name: tab-browser-ultimate
description: Embedded browser tab with AI capabilities, Claude and Codex integration

commands.title: Connect Claude Code to This Browser (MCP)
Add Element XPath to Claude Code
Add CSS Path to Claude Code
Add Console Output to Claude Code

tabBrowser.files.reloadOnChange.markdownDescription: Reload the panel when a local file it is showing — or one that page pulled in — is saved. Only files the page actually asked for are watched, and only pages opened from disk: a page served by a dev server has that server's own reload.

tabBrowser.contextMenu.enabled.markdownDescription: Answer a right-click in the page with this panel's own menu: copy the element that was clicked, hand it to an assistant, or open the editor's developer tools. A page that defines a context menu of its own keeps it, and turning this off leaves every right-click to the editor.

enumDescriptions: Write the path to a file and @-mention it, which lands in the conversation you already have open
Open a new conversation with the path already in its prompt box, unsent
tabBrowser.claude.pathDelivery.markdownDescription: How "Add element XPath / path to Claude Code" delivers the path. Claude Code only accepts an `@`-mention of a file into an open conversation; plain text can only be pre-filled when a new conversation is created. The full element report always goes as a file.

enumDescriptions: Only urls a dev server prints, i.e. localhost and the loopback addresses
Every http and https url printed in a terminal
Leave terminal links to the editor, which opens them in an external browser
tabBrowser.terminalLinks.mode.markdownDescription: Which urls in the terminal `Cmd`/`Ctrl` + click opens in this browser panel instead of an external browser.

tabBrowser.mcp.enabled.markdownDescription: Run a local mcp server that lets an assistant read and drive the browser panel. It listens on the loopback interface only and requires a token, which the **Connect Claude Code to This Browser** command hands over. VS Code's own chat is told about it automatically.

tabBrowser.mcp.port.markdownDescription: Port for the mcp server. A fixed port keeps a Claude Code configuration valid across restarts; when it is taken — by another window, for instance — the next free one is used.

tabBrowser.showPageIcon.description: Show the icon of the loaded page on the panel's tab. The icon is downloaded from the page's own server; turn this off to keep the browser panel from making that request.

tabBrowser.copyAsFile.markdownDescription: Put multi-line copies (the element report and console output) on the clipboard as a temporary file next to their text, so pasting them into a chat attaches a document. Falls back to plain text on platforms without clipboard file support, in remote workspaces, and for one-line copies such as "Copy element XPath".

tabBrowser.notifyOnCopy.description: Show a notification after the copy menu has written to the clipboard. When disabled only a status bar message is shown.

enumDescriptions: Full element context: descriptor, url, html path, outer html, dimensions and the css that applies
CSS selector, e.g. #root > main > ul > li:nth-of-type(3)
CSS selector and XPath on two lines
Full JSON payload with selector, xpath, tag, attributes, dimensions and styles
tabBrowser.picker.copyFormat.description: What "Copy element" writes to the clipboard. "Copy element XPath" always writes an XPath.

tabBrowser.picker.keepActiveAfterPick.description: Keep element picking enabled after an element has been picked.

tabBrowser.picker.preferAttributes.description: Attributes that are preferred over structural selectors when building an element path.

enumDescriptions: Route localhost urls through the local instrumenting proxy; other urls are only proxied once the copy menu needs them
Always route http/https urls through the local instrumenting proxy
Never use the proxy. The copy menu will not be available
tabBrowser.proxy.mode.markdownDescription: The copy menu requires the page to be served through a local proxy that injects a small script, because a cross-origin `iframe` can be neither inspected nor read from the webview.

tabBrowser.proxy.log.markdownDescription: Log every request the local proxy answers to an output channel ("AI Browser proxy"): the method, the path, the status, and the *names* of the cookies forwarded upstream. Useful for the one question the panel cannot otherwise answer — whether a request the page made went through the proxy at all. A request that is missing from the log left it, which is what breaks a login when a page asks for its own api by absolute url.

tabBrowser.proxy.ignoreCertificateErrors.description: Ignore TLS certificate errors when the proxy talks to an https target (useful for local dev servers with self-signed certificates).

scripts.test: node test/proxy.test.mjs && node test/config-lock.test.mjs && node test/host.test.mjs
scripts.publish:all: npm run package && npm run publish && npm run publish:ovsx
